name: Yakisugi
tagline: Full-spectrum infrared sauna in charred Western Red Cedar.
description: The OneBase Yakisugi is the centrepiece sauna. Western Red Cedar finished with the Japanese Yakisugi charring technique gives a matte-black exterior that is naturally resistant to moisture, bacteria and wear. Inside, low-EMF full-spectrum infrared runs at a restorative 135–149°F, and the whole unit plugs into a standard outlet with no plumbing.

highlights.title: Architectural Yakisugi finish
highlights.body: Charred cedar is a visual differentiator and a carbonised layer that resists moisture, bacteria and wear. Essential for high-traffic hygiene.

highlights.title: Full-spectrum depth
highlights.body: Low-EMF panels deliver near, mid and far infrared to penetrate deeper into muscle tissue for recovery and metabolic detox.

highlights.title: Plug-and-play integration
highlights.body: Modular, no-plumbing architecture drops a premium thermal suite into any room with a standard electrical outlet.

highlights.title: High-traffic durability
highlights.body: Heavy-duty tempered glass and reinforced commercial-grade components, built to run 12+ hours a day.

highlights.title: The comfort advantage
highlights.body: A tolerable 135–149°F range lowers the heat-shock barrier for new users, increasing accessibility and frequency of use.

electrical.label: Supply
electrical.value: Standard electrical outlet; confirm circuit rating by size at quotation

faqs.a: Infrared panels heat your body directly rather than the surrounding air, giving a sauna experience at a more comfortable air temperature.

faqs.q: How does infrared differ from a traditional sauna?
faqs.a: Traditional saunas heat the air to 150–195°F. Infrared uses radiant heat that penetrates muscles, joints and tissues in a gentler environment while still improving circulation, recovery and relaxation.

faqs.q: Is the Yakisugi finish just aesthetic?
faqs.a: No. Charring creates a richly textured matte surface that is highly resistant to moisture and wear, which is exactly what busy wellness environments need.

faqs.q: Can I combine sauna with other treatments?
faqs.a: Yes. Infrared saunas pair with cold therapy such as the IceVault, massage, red light, HBOT or meditation. Hydrate and cool down between treatments.
Yes. They typically use less energy than traditional saunas or steam rooms while delivering the full therapeutic benefits.
